governanceNotes: D1 batch 65 (2026-09-26): one bounded association edge authored - occipital-neuralgia to migraine-headaches (rank 1) - classified ASSOCIATION_ONLY with etiologicalConsensus NOT_ESTABLISHED, vaNexusProbabilityAlignment NOT_ASSERTED, and hypothesizedOnly:true. The proposition rests on the 800-patient headache-clinic prevalence study with up to 85 percent ON comorbidity and the ON-aggravates-comorbid-headache framing (PMID 33968466) and the refractory-ON decompression series with universal comorbid-headache improvement after nerve decompression (PMID 38090265).

Counter-evidence and caveat screens recorded 2026-09-26: (i) direction - the only quantified adjusted odds ratio runs chronic migraine to ON odds (aOR 2.190), so this edge's direction rests on the authors' aggravation framing and the decompression dechallenge rather than a quantified forward estimate; (ii) evidence class - one retrospective clinic study plus one uncontrolled 15-patient surgical series with regression-to-the-mean exposure; (iii) semantic boundary - ON pain is nerve-irritation-explained and was NOT authored as unexplained chronic pain despite refractory courses (the family's earlier neuralgia-to-pain edges had diagnostically-unexplained courses as their basis); (iv) comorbidity dominance - only 15 percent of ON is isolated, so most ON care occurs within mixed headache populations where attribution is inherently uncertain.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: Occipital neuralgia is associated with comorbid migraine and with aggravation of coexisting headache at headache-clinic prevalence and surgical-dechallenge level: the community headache-clinic prevalence study of 800 patients found occipital neuralgia in nearly 25 percent with only 15 percent of ON cases isolated, up to 85 percent occurring with an additional headache type most commonly migraine, and states that undiagnosed or inadequately treated ON can increase the frequency and intensity of other comorbid headache disorders (PMID 33968466), and the refractory-ON decompression case series of 15 patients found all patients reporting improvement of comorbid headache disorders, most commonly migraine, after greater occipital nerve decompression alongside ON symptom relief (PMID 38090265); recorded as documented association only with the reverse-direction signal carried openly.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation is established for any individual: the prevalence study's quantified direction runs from chronic migraine to elevated odds of ON (adjusted OR 2.19), so the migraine-to-ON pathway is at least as well supported as the reverse aggravation claim, and individual claims require individual headache-specialist attribution with medication-overuse, cervicogenic, and tension-type exclusion.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: Greater occipital nerve irritation with afferent convergence on the trigeminocervical complex drives central sensitization that amplifies and worsens coexisting migraine so increased migraine frequency and intensity result, the convergence-aggravation route consistent with the decompression dechallenge in which comorbid migraine improved when occipital nerve compression was relieved, but whether this route produced any individual migraine worsening remains hypothesized until headache-diary and examination records are reviewed.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: The association is supported at single headache-clinic prevalence study plus 15-patient surgical case series class only: the prevalence study is retrospective from one community clinic, its quantified risk direction runs migraine-to-ON rather than the reverse, and the aggravation claim is author commentary rather than a measured endpoint; the decompression series is uncontrolled with regression to the mean possible.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: The quantified adjusted odds ratio runs chronic migraine to ON odds (aOR 2.19), reverse to this edge's direction; the ON-to-headache-worsening claim is stated in commentary rather than measured; the decompression series is uncontrolled with referral-selection toward refractory cases and regression to the mean; ON diagnosis is clinical with variable Tinel-sign sensitivity; and medication-overuse headache, cervicogenic headache, and tension-type headache compete for individual attribution.
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: medication-overuse headache from frequent analgesic use in refractory cases
cervicogenic headache from cervical spine disease
migraine chronification independent of ON (the reverse-direction signal: chronic migraine raised ON odds)
post-traumatic headache with occipital nerve involvement

evidenceGaps: The quantified adjusted odds ratio runs chronic migraine to ON odds (aOR 2.19), reverse to this edge's direction; the ON-to-headache-worsening claim is stated in commentary rather than measured; the decompression series is uncontrolled with referral-selection toward refractory cases and regression to the mean; ON diagnosis is clinical with variable Tinel-sign sensitivity; and medication-overuse headache, cervicogenic headache, and tension-type headache compete for individual attribution.
suggestions.rationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY at prevalence-study plus surgical-dechallenge class with the reverse-direction signal carried openly: the 800-patient headache-clinic study found ON in nearly 25 percent with up to 85 percent comorbid with other headache types and documented the aggravation framing (PMID 33968466), and the refractory-ON decompression series found comorbid migraine improvement after nerve decompression in all 15 patients (PMID 38090265); because the quantified direction runs migraine-to-ON (aOR 2.19) and the aggravation claim is commentary-level with an uncontrolled dechallenge, the conservative standard keeps the edge at association only and routes individual claims through dated headache-diary and examination review with medication-overuse, cervicogenic, and tension-type exclusion.

sourceReferences.citation: Mathew PG, Najib U, Khaled S, et al. Prevalence of Occipital Neuralgia at a Community Hospital-based Headache Clinic Neurol Clin Pract. 2021 Feb;11(1):6-12. PMID 33968466.
sourceReferences.note: Community hospital headache-clinic prevalence study of 800 patients (Neurol Clin Pract 2021): ON in 195 (nearly 25%); isolated ON only 15.38% of ON cases so up to 85% had a coexisting headache type; chronic migraine raised odds of ON (aOR 2.190, 1.364-3.515) - reverse-direction signal; authors state undiagnosed/undertreated ON can increase frequency and intensity of comorbid headache disorders; supports the bounded association and aggravation framing only.
sourceReferences.sourceLocator: PMID 33968466; results (ON prevalence, comorbidity, and odds ratios)

sourceReferences.citation: Austen WG Jr, Remy K, Packowski K, et al. Refractory occipital neuralgia treatment with nerve decompression surgery: a case series Front Neurol. 2023;14:1284101. PMID 38090265.
sourceReferences.note: Prospective case series of 15 refractory ON patients undergoing greater occipital nerve decompression (Front Neurol 2023): preoperative median 30 headache days/month, intensity 8, duration 24h after trials of 10 nerve blocks and 11.7 botox cycles; postoperative headache days 5, intensity 4 (p<0.01); ALL patients reported improvement of comorbid headache disorders, most commonly migraine; supports the bounded dechallenge association only.
